analyst_view.overall: Early view: Napoli are tenth with five points from their last five games, and one report describes tension around the club even though Allegri has been backed; Noa Lang has fallen out with the fans after the Lazio draw. They go to Manchester City three days later. Torino lost 15 players to international duty, the most in Serie A, and Abate complained about a lack of energy in the final third after the 1-1 with Lecce.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Napoli's games have often been open (3-3 with Roma, 4-1 at Monza), but they have scored only once, an own goal, in their last two, and one Italian commentator compared their slow build-up to city traffic. Torino took only nine shots at home to Lecce, so the factors cancel out and I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 9.4 corners. I lean slightly higher: Napoli's home games average almost 11 corners, and against Lazio they relied on crosses and direct play to get back in the game. Torino's away matches have averaged under nine, so this is a small lean.

cards.text: The numbers already say only 3.0 cards, and I lean a little lower still. Torino's games average about 2.2 cards, the fewest in the league, and Napoli's about 2.7. Neither side plays a pressing, physical game that produces bookings.

shots.text: The site expects 27.8 shots. I lean slightly higher, because Napoli's home games have averaged over 31 shots, with both sides shooting a lot. Torino give up almost 18 shots a game away, and Napoli tend to shoot from distance when they cannot get through.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Napoli's home games and Torino's away games both average a little over nine, but Torino rarely hit the target themselves, so I stay with the number.
